name: Style the control
description: Learn how a headless switch gets its look from data-state, and when slot attrs belong on your element.

steps.title: It has a look
steps.task: This switch is colored and it moves. The component did not paint that. The example did.
steps.learn: See that the look lives in the example

steps.title: The attribute flipped
steps.task: We turned it on. The thumb slid because data-state changed to checked. Nothing in script toggled a class.

steps.title: The class that moved it
steps.task: We opened the source. The thumb is translate-x-1 until data-state is checked, then translate-x-6. The attribute flip is the animation.
steps.learn: Find the data-state class in the example source

steps.title: Style the attribute
steps.task: data-state is checked, unchecked, or indeterminate. Write CSS against that. Do not mirror it with a class you toggle yourself.
steps.learn: Prefer data-state over a scripted class

steps.title: Absent means off
steps.task: data-disabled is the value true, or the attribute is missing. A false value would still match a data-disabled selector, so the component omits it instead.
steps.learn: See why boolean data attributes are true or absent

steps.title: Two channels
steps.task: aria-checked is for assistive tech. data-state is for CSS. Mixed is data-state indeterminate with aria-checked false.
steps.learn: Keep ARIA and data-state on their own jobs

steps.title: Bind attrs once
steps.task: This fence is renderless, so attrs goes on the element you render. On the default button, attrs is already on the root. Binding it again on a child fires the click twice.
steps.learn: Bind slot attrs only on a renderless host

steps.title: That's the look
steps.task: The component ships the state. You paint data-state. Bind attrs to your own element only when you took the element away.
steps.learn: Style the next headless control the same way
